title: Connected TV Attribution & Incrementality: Complete Measurement Guide for DTC Brands

facts.fact: The guide says DTC brands investing $50K or more monthly in CTV need to prove incrementality and true attribution to scale profitably.
facts.quote: For DTC brands investing $50K+ monthly in CTV, proving incrementality and understanding true attribution is critical for scaling campaigns profitably.

facts.fact: The author states the guide is based on $75M or more in annual CTV spend across 200 or more DTC campaigns (vendor's own experience, not third-party data).
facts.quote: based on $75M+ in annual CTV spend across 200+ DTC campaigns

facts.fact: The guide claims platform reporting often shows 40-70% lower CTV conversions than reality (unsourced claim).
facts.quote: Platform reporting often shows 40-70% lower conversions than reality

facts.fact: The guide recommends extended CTV attribution windows of 14 to 30+ days because traditional 1-day windows miss most conversions.
facts.quote: Need for extended attribution periods (14-30+ days)

facts.fact: The guide recommends CTV view-through attribution of 14-30 days in its example attribution window configuration.
The guide's example configuration sets search attribution to a 30-day click window.
The Marketing Mix Modeling section says the model needs at least 2 years of daily sales data.
The geo-holdout test design calls for choosing at least 20 matched market pairs.
The guide says a geo-holdout test typically needs at least $100K in monthly spend to have sufficient statistical power.
facts.quote: Ensure sufficient statistical power (typically need $100K+ monthly spend)

facts.fact: The geo-holdout control group has CTV advertising paused or reduced by 50-80%.
facts.quote: Control Group: CTV advertising paused or reduced by 50-80%

facts.fact: The geo-holdout test should run at least 6 to 12 weeks for statistical significance.
facts.quote: Duration: 6-12 weeks minimum for statistical significance

facts.fact: The guide sets a p-value threshold below 0.05 for determining statistical significance in geo tests.
In the audience segment test, heavy exposure is defined as 8 or more CTV impressions per person per week.
facts.quote: **Heavy Exposure:** 8+ impressions per person per week

facts.fact: In the audience segment test, medium exposure is defined as 4-7 CTV impressions per person per week.
facts.quote: **Medium Exposure:** 4-7 impressions per person per week

facts.fact: In the audience segment test, light exposure is defined as 1-3 CTV impressions per person per week.
facts.quote: **Light Exposure:** 1-3 impressions per person per week

facts.fact: The guide lists a 14-day primary attribution window as an industry benchmark for beauty and skincare.
The guide states a 28-day extended window for beauty and skincare captures 85% or more of conversions.
The guide lists a 21-day primary attribution window as an industry benchmark for apparel.
The guide lists a 30-day primary attribution window as an industry benchmark for home and garden.
The guide's linear time-decay example gives full attribution value on day 1, 50% on day 7, and 0% on day 14.
In the daypart test example, late-night CTV spend (11 PM-1 AM) is reduced by 50%.
facts.quote: Late Night (11 PM-1 AM): 50% spend reduction

facts.fact: The page gives a time-decay attribution schedule in which a CTV conversion on day 1 gets 100% attribution value, falling to 12.5% by day 14.
facts.value: 100% on day 1; 50% on day 3; 25% on day 7; 12.5% on day 14
facts.quote: Day 1: 100% attribution value Day 3: 50% attribution value Day 7: 25% attribution value Day 14: 12.5% attribution value

facts.fact: The page states that deterministic cross-device matching typically achieves a 40-60% match rate.
The page states that probabilistic cross-device matching typically achieves a 60-80% match rate.
The page states that a combined deterministic and probabilistic approach can achieve a 70-85% match rate.
In its beauty brand case study, the brand's monthly CTV spend was $300K.
facts.quote: Case Study 1: Beauty Brand ($300K Monthly CTV Spend)

facts.fact: In the beauty brand case study, traditional attribution showed 1.2x ROAS for CTV.
In the beauty brand case study, the brand ran a 12-week geo-holdout test across 40 matched markets.
In the beauty brand case study, the agency reported true incremental ROAS of 2.8x, which it said was 133% higher than platform reporting.
facts.quote: True incremental ROAS: 2.8x (133% higher than platform reporting)

facts.fact: In the home goods case study, the brand's monthly CTV spend was $150K.
facts.quote: Case Study 2: Home Goods Brand ($150K Monthly CTV Spend)

facts.fact: In the home goods case study, the agency found that 60% of CTV-driven sales occurred after day 14.
facts.quote: Discovered 60% of CTV-driven sales occurred after day 14

facts.fact: In the home goods case study, true ROAS increased from 1.8x to 3.1x with proper attribution.
facts.quote: True ROAS increased from 1.8x to 3.1x with proper attribution

facts.fact: In the home goods case study, the agency identified an optimal frequency of 4-6 exposures per month.
facts.quote: Identified optimal frequency: 4-6 exposures per month

facts.fact: In the supplement brand case study, the brand's monthly CTV spend was $500K.
facts.quote: Case Study 3: Supplement Brand ($500K Monthly CTV Spend)

facts.fact: In the supplement brand case study, CTV-acquired customers had 40% higher LTV.
In the supplement brand case study, the optimal attribution window was 28 days.
The page recommends a minimum of $50K+ monthly CTV spend for basic attribution.
The page recommends a minimum of $100K+ monthly spend for incrementality testing.
The page recommends a minimum of $200K+ monthly spend across all channels for marketing mix modeling.
facts.quote: **Marketing Mix Modeling:** $200K+ monthly across all channels

facts.fact: The page recommends a minimum of $300K+ monthly spend for advanced geo-testing.
The page suggests that 5-10% of CTV spend should go to measurement tools.
facts.quote: **5-10%** of CTV spend should go to measurement tools

facts.fact: The page gives a professional MMM cost range of $50-150K annually.
The page gives an attribution platform cost of $2-5K monthly.
The page gives a testing tools cost of $3-8K monthly.
The page claims that in Year 1 measurement investment yields a 20-40% improvement in ROAS understanding.
The page claims that in Year 1 measurement investment gives confidence to scale CTV by 50-100%.
ATTN Agency states that properly attributed CTV campaigns typically show 2-4x higher ROAS than platform reporting suggests.
facts.quote: properly attributed CTV campaigns typically show 2-4x higher ROAS than platform reporting suggests, leading to significant budget reallocation opportunities
